Otherwise it classifies non-associated items: it checks `def_kind` and `is_intrinsic` to build an intrinsic instance, checks `lang_items().drop_in_place_fn()` for drop glue, uses `type_at`, `needs_drop`, and `kind` to decide whether to construct nontrivial or trivial `DropGlue`, and falls back to a regular `Item` instance for free items.

compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/instance.rs.signature: fn resolve_associated_item<'tcx>( tcx: TyCtxt<'tcx>, trait_item_id: DefId, param_env: ty::ParamEnv<'tcx>, trait_id: DefId, rcvr_substs: SubstsRef<'tcx>, ) -> Result<Option<Instance<'tcx>>, ErrorGuaranteed> {
compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/instance.rs.summary: Resolves a trait-associated item to the concrete impl or vtable entry used for codegen. It builds the receiver trait reference with `from_method`, packages it with `as_query_input`, and calls `codegen_select_candidate` to choose an implementation. For user-defined impls, it calls `trait_id_of_impl`, `trait_def`, `ancestors`, and `leaf_def` to map the trait item to the impl item, checks specialization eligibility with `is_final` and `still_further_specializable`, computes impl arguments via `rebase_onto` and `translate_args`, and validates the result with `check_args_compatible` and `compare_impl_const` before constructing the final `Instance`. Along the way it also uses queries such as `predicates_of`/`instantiate`, rigidity checks like `is_known_rigid`, and delayed-bug diagnostics via `dcx`, `span_delayed_bug`, and `def_span` when an associated item should not be codegen-reachable.
Registers this file’s query provider by installing `resolve_instance_raw` into the `Providers` table.

method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/collect/: Finds hidden-type constraints for a type-alias `impl Trait` by computing its defining HIR scope and traversing that scope with `TaitConstraintLocator`, using `walk_toplevel_module` for crate scope or explicitly calling `visit_item`, `visit_impl_item`, `visit_trait_item`, or `visit_foreign_item` on the defining node so sibling defining uses are included. It then cross-checks the chosen hidden type against collected `typeck_types` via `build_mismatch_error`, and reports an unconstrained opaque if nothing constrained it.

Per-item constraint checker for TAIT/associated opaque discovery: it skips items without typeck results, rejects `_`-inferred function returns by creating an error type, reads `typeck` results, filters `concrete_opaque_types` down to the target opaque, records typeck-visible hidden types, validates the item against `opaque_types_defined_by`, and then uses `mir_borrowck` to obtain the region-precise hidden type. When multiple defining uses disagree, it reports the mismatch with `build_mismatch_error` and updates or preserves `self.found` accordingly.
Returns the HIR map from `self.tcx.hir()` so `TaitConstraintLocator` can recursively traverse nested HIR nodes.
Visits expressions for TAIT constraint discovery; when it sees a closure, it calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the closure's `def_id`, then continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_expr`.

Visits an item in the TAIT reveal scope, skipping the opaque item itself; for every other item it calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the item's `def_id` and then recurses with `intravisit::walk_item`.
Visits an impl item during TAIT constraint search, skips the opaque item itself, calls `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on other impl items, and then continues with `intravisit::walk_impl_item`.
Visits a trait item for TAIT constraint collection by calling `TaitConstraintLocator::check` on the trait item's `def_id` and then recursing with `intravisit::walk_trait_item`.

Computes the hidden type for a return-position `impl Trait` by first scanning `typeck(owner_def_id).concrete_opaque_types` for the target opaque, normalizing each candidate with `remap_generic_params_to_declaration_params`, and using `build_mismatch_error` to stash HIR-level inconsistencies. It then queries `mir_borrowck(owner_def_id)` for the authoritative hidden type and, if present, traverses the owner body with `intravisit::walk_item`, `walk_impl_item`, or `walk_trait_item` using `RpitConstraintChecker` so nested bodies can be checked for mismatching constraints; otherwise it returns an error or diverging default type.

Checks one nested body for RPIT consistency by reading `mir_borrowck(def_id).concrete_opaque_types`, filtering to the target opaque, and comparing each discovered hidden type against `self.found`; on disagreement it reports the mismatch via `build_mismatch_error` and emits the diagnostic.
Returns `self.tcx.hir()` as the nested visit map so `RpitConstraintChecker` can traverse nested HIR structure.
Visits expressions while checking RPIT constraints; for closures it calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the closure's `def_id`, then continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_expr`.
Visits an item in RPIT checking, skipping the opaque item itself; for every other item it calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the item's `def_id` and then recurses with `intravisit::walk_item`.
Visits an impl item during RPIT checking, skips the opaque item itself, calls `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on other impl items, and continues traversal with `intravisit::walk_impl_item`.
Visits a trait item for RPIT checking by calling `RpitConstraintChecker::check` on the trait item's `def_id` and then recursing with `intravisit::walk_trait_item`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_infer/src/infer/opaque_ty: Scans a foldable value for local opaque aliases that are currently definable in this context, replaces each eligible opaque with a fresh inference type variable, and accumulates the resulting obligations. It first short-circuits when `next_trait_solver` is enabled or `has_opaque_types` is false, and for each matched opaque it calls `opaque_type_origin` to decide eligibility and `handle_opaque_type` to relate the new inference variable back to the opaque definition.

Handles the relation between an opaque type and another type during inference, ignoring error types, orienting the comparison by `a_is_expected`, and only treating local opaque aliases as definitional when they are valid for the current `DefiningAnchor`. When the opaque is allowed to be defined here, it calls `opaque_type_origin` to validate the defining context and then calls `register_hidden_type` to record the inferred hidden type; otherwise it emits diagnostics for invalid defining-use situations such as problematic opaque-to-opaque cases.

Resolves the concrete hidden type, computes the invariant lifetime arguments of the opaque plus `'static` as the allowed choice set, and visits the hidden type to constrain every free region to one of those choices. It calls `member_constraint` through the region visitor callback for each discovered region.

Determines whether a local opaque type is being defined from the current defining-use anchor and, if so, returns its `OpaqueTyOrigin`. For type-alias opaques it checks associated-type definitions via `opaque_types_defined_by` and otherwise calls `may_define_opaque_type` to decide whether the current item may define the opaque.
Visits inside binders without stopping, delegating traversal to `super_visit_with` and then continuing.
Processes each encountered region for opaque-member checking, skipping bound regions and invoking the stored callback for all other regions.

Traverses only types that contain free regions and selectively visits the parts relevant for opaque lifetime constraints. It skips enclosing-item lifetimes for closures and coroutines by manually visiting captured/upvar and signature-related components, visits only non-bivariant arguments of nested opaque aliases, and otherwise falls back to `super_visit_with`.
Returns whether this `UseKind` represents a defining use, yielding true for `DefiningUse` and false for `OpaqueUse`.

Registers an inferred hidden type for an opaque definition and produces the obligations needed to justify it. It calls `insert_hidden_type` to store or unify the hidden type in the opaque-type table, then calls `add_item_bounds_for_hidden_type` to add the opaque item's declared bounds as obligations on that hidden type.

Inserts a hidden type candidate into inference state for an opaque key. In intercrate mode it adds an ambiguous obligation instead of defining the opaque; otherwise it registers the hidden type in the opaque storage, and if a previous hidden type was already present it calls `eq_exp` to equate the old and new hidden types and extends the obligation list with the resulting obligations.

Instantiates the explicit bounds declared on an opaque item, rewrites them so they apply to the inferred hidden type, and pushes each rewritten predicate as an obligation. While folding each predicate, it calls `infer_projection` to replace eligible projection aliases with inference variables, and it substitutes self-references to the same opaque alias with `hidden_ty` before creating obligations.
Checks whether a named opaque type may be defined from the given local item by walking up the HIR parent chain from the item to see whether it reaches the opaque type’s defining scope.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_trait_selection/src/trait: Trait method contract for shallow normalization of a foldable value, returning the normalized value plus any generated obligations. It does not call other methods in this list.

Implements shallow normalization for `At`: it either returns the input unchanged under the next trait solver, or creates a selection context and calls `normalize_with_depth` to normalize the value and collect obligations.
Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Ambiguous`; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Sets the candidate set to `ProjectionCandidateSet::Error(err)` to record a selection failure; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Adds a projection candidate when possible, deduplicates identical candidates, prefers `ParamEnv` candidates over others, and otherwise converts a conflicting single candidate into ambiguity. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Handles higher-ranked projection equality by instantiating the obligation binder with placeholders inside a probe and then calling `project_and_unify_type`. It converts mismatches into `MismatchedProjectionTypes` and, when experimenting with extended GATs, filters out obligations that mention the newly created universe before returning `Holds`.

Solves a concrete projection equality by first calling `opt_normalize_projection_type` to normalize the projection, then replacing opaque types in the expected term with inference variables, and finally equating the normalized and expected terms. It returns `Holds` with accumulated obligations on success, or reports failed normalization, recursion, or mismatched projection types.

Convenience entry point for normalization at a given recursion depth: it allocates an obligation buffer, calls `normalize_with_depth_to`, and packages the normalized value together with the collected obligations.

Normalizes a foldable value into a caller-provided obligation buffer by constructing an `AssocTypeNormalizer` with `AssocTypeNormalizer::new` and then calling its `fold` method under stack protection.

Like `normalize_with_depth_to`, but uses a normalizer configured to avoid eager inference replacement: it calls `AssocTypeNormalizer::new_without_eager_inference_replacement` and then invokes `AssocTypeNormalizer::fold` under stack protection.

Checks whether a value contains projection-, inherent-, const-projection-, or optionally opaque-related type flags that require normalization, depending on the `Reveal` mode. It does not call other methods in this list.
Constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` configured for normal eager inference replacement, after asserting the old trait solver path is in use. It does not call other methods in this list.
Constructs an `AssocTypeNormalizer` configured to avoid eager inference replacement. It does not call other methods in this list.

Top-level normalization helper for the normalizer: it resolves inference variables, asserts there are no escaping bound vars, calls `needs_normalization` to fast-path already-normal values, and otherwise recursively folds the value.
Returns the type context used by the normalizer's folder implementation. It does not call other methods in this list.
Tracks entry into and exit from a binder while folding by pushing binder state, recursively folding the binder contents, and then popping the state. It does not call other methods in this list.

Core type normalization routine for the old projection engine. It first calls `needs_normalization`, recursively folds nested structure, normalizes revealed opaque types, and handles alias types by using `normalize_projection_type` or `opt_normalize_projection_type` for associated projections, `normalize_inherent_projection` for inherent aliases, and `with_replaced_escaping_bound_vars` when escaping bound vars must be temporarily replaced across normalization.

Normalizes constants when needed for the old solver path: after checking feature gating and `needs_normalization`, it recursively folds the constant and then calls `with_replaced_escaping_bound_vars`, whose callback invokes const normalization on the folded value.

Recursively normalizes a predicate only when normalization is allowed and `needs_normalization` reports work to do; otherwise it leaves the predicate unchanged. It explicitly calls `needs_normalization`.

Utility that temporarily replaces escaping bound vars with placeholders before running a closure, then restores them afterward. When escaping vars are present it calls `BoundVarReplacer::replace_bound_vars`, runs the callback, and then calls `PlaceholderReplacer::replace_placeholders`; otherwise it just runs the callback directly.

Entry point for converting bound regions, types, and consts into placeholders while recording reverse mappings. It constructs a `BoundVarReplacer`, folds the input through it, and returns the rewritten value plus the collected maps.
Finds or lazily creates the universe index associated with a given de Bruijn level, extending the tracked universe stack as necessary. It does not call other methods in this list.
Returns the type context used by the bound-variable replacer. It does not call other methods in this list.
Updates the current de Bruijn index while recursively folding inside a binder, then restores it afterward. It does not call other methods in this list.

Rewrites late-bound regions at or above the current binder depth into placeholder regions, recording the mapping and using `BoundVarReplacer::universe_for` to choose the correct universe. Other regions are left unchanged.

Rewrites bound types at or above the current binder depth into placeholder types, recording the mapping and calling `BoundVarReplacer::universe_for` to obtain the universe; otherwise it recursively folds only when nested bound vars may still be present.

Rewrites bound consts at or above the current binder depth into placeholder consts, recording the mapping and calling `BoundVarReplacer::universe_for` to select the universe; otherwise it recursively folds the const.
Recursively folds a predicate only when it still contains bound vars at or above the current binder depth; otherwise it returns the predicate unchanged. It does not call other methods in this list.
Entry point for converting placeholders back into bound vars using previously recorded maps and universe information. It constructs a `PlaceholderReplacer` and folds the input through it.
Returns the type context used by the placeholder replacer. It does not call other methods in this list.

Avoids unnecessary work for binders without placeholders or infer regions; otherwise it adjusts binder depth, recursively folds the binder contents, and restores the depth afterward. It does not call other methods in this list.

Resolves region inference variables, then replaces placeholder regions with late-bound regions using the stored mapping and universe/de Bruijn translation; otherwise leaves the region unchanged. It recursively calls `fold_region` through the folder traversal machinery when nested folding occurs.

Rewrites placeholder types into bound types using the stored placeholder-to-bound mapping and computed de Bruijn index. If the type is not a direct placeholder but still contains placeholders or infer-regions, it explicitly calls `super_fold_with` to continue recursive folding into substructure.

Rewrites placeholder consts into bound consts using the stored mapping and translated de Bruijn index, preserving the const's type. For non-placeholder consts, it explicitly calls `super_fold_with` to recursively fold nested contents.

Public entry point that normalizes an associated-type projection to a `Term`. It explicitly calls `opt_normalize_projection_type`; if that returns no concrete result due to ambiguity, it falls back to `infer_projection` to create an inference variable and deferred obligations.

Attempts to normalize a projection type with recursion detection and projection-cache support, returning either a concrete normalized term, ambiguity, or in-progress recursion. It explicitly calls `project` to compute the projection when cache lookup does not decide the result, and then records progress, ambiguity, or errors back into the cache while extending the caller's obligations.

Produces an error-tolerant normalized term by creating a fresh type or const inference variable and adding the projected trait obligation so trait solving can continue. It does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Normalizes an inherent associated type by checking recursion depth, computing impl arguments, adding instantiated predicates as obligations, and normalizing the resulting type if it still contains aliases. It calls `compute_inherent_assoc_ty_args`.

Computes the substitution list for an inherent associated type by creating fresh impl generics, normalizing the impl’s self type, and unifying that normalized impl type with the projection’s self type to infer impl parameters, collecting any generated obligations. It explicitly calls `normalize_with_depth_to` to normalize the impl type before unification.
Constructs a `Progress` value whose term is an error type and whose obligations list is empty; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.
Appends additional obligations to an existing `Progress` result and returns it; it does not call any other method from the Methods List.

Top-level projection solver that checks recursion and prior errors, assembles candidates from the parameter environment, trait definition, object bounds, and impl selection, then either confirms a unique candidate or returns ambiguity/error/no-progress. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_param_env`, `assemble_candidates_from_trait_def`, `assemble_candidates_from_object_ty`, `assemble_candidates_from_impls`, `confirm_candidate`, `Progress::error`, and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`/`ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error` indirectly through candidate assembly outcomes.

Builds a projection candidate for an impl-trait-in-trait associated item by deriving the parent trait predicate and attempting selection with `select` inside `commit_if_ok`. On success it records `ProjectionCandidate::ImplTraitInTrait` via `push_candidate`; on uncertainty it calls `mark_ambiguous`, and on selection failure it calls `mark_error`.
Collects projection candidates from the caller bounds in the parameter environment. It calls `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Scans item bounds from the trait definition for matching projection clauses, pushes matching trait-definition candidates, and marks ambiguity when matching cannot be decided. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Builds projection candidates from object type projection bounds when the trait supports object-based projection, and marks ambiguity if the self type is still a type variable. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `assemble_candidates_from_predicates`.

Filters a stream of projection predicates by associated item and argument compatibility, probes whether each can match the goal, and either pushes a candidate or marks ambiguity. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::push_candidate` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous`.

Selects the underlying trait obligation to derive impl-based projection candidates, then records ambiguity, selection error, or a usable builtin/user-defined candidate while accounting for specialization and builtin trait cases. It calls `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_ambiguous` and `ProjectionCandidateSet::mark_error`.

Turns a chosen projection candidate into concrete projected progress by delegating to the appropriate confirmation routine and then opportunistically resolving inferred regions in the resulting term. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` for `ParamEnv`, `Object`, and `TraitDef` candidates, and `confirm_select_candidate` for `Select` candidates.

Confirms an impl-selected candidate by dispatching to the appropriate builtin or user-defined confirmation path based on the selected impl source and trait kind. It calls `confirm_impl_candidate`, `confirm_coroutine_candidate`, `confirm_future_candidate`, `confirm_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_async_iterator_candidate`, `confirm_closure_candidate`, `confirm_fn_pointer_candidate`, `confirm_async_closure_candidate`, `confirm_async_fn_kind_helper_candidate`, and `confirm_builtin_candidate`.

Handles projection for generator associated types (`Yield`/`Return`) by resolving the obligation self type as a generator, normalizing its generator signature with `normalize_with_depth`, building the corresponding generator projection predicate via `generator_trait_ref_and_outputs`, and then delegating final confirmation to `confirm_param_env_candidate`. It returns that result augmented with the incoming nested obligations and the obligations produced during signature normalization via `with_addl_obligations`.

Computes the `Future::Output` projection from the normalized coroutine signature of an async future and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Resolves built-in associated type projections such as discriminant, async destructor, or pointee metadata, building any extra obligations needed, then confirms the resulting projection through the param-env path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.
Normalizes a function pointer signature and confirms its callable output projection via the shared callable path. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.

Builds the effective callable signature for closures or coroutine-closures, including async/coroutine-specific output construction when needed, then confirms the resulting callable projection. It calls `confirm_callable_candidate` and `Progress::with_addl_obligations`.
Constructs the `FnOnce::Output` projection predicate from a callable signature and confirms it through the param-env projection path. It calls `confirm_param_env_candidate`.

Confirms a projection candidate taken from the parameter environment by instantiating the cached binder, normalizing the obligation projection and optionally the candidate projection with `normalize_with_depth_to`, equating the two projections via inference, and on success extending obligations and calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations`; on failure it returns an error term.

Confirms a projection candidate coming from a selected impl by locating the associated item in the impl, rebasing and translating trait/impl arguments, building the resulting associated term from the impl item definition, checking argument compatibility, and then calling `assoc_ty_own_obligations` before instantiating the term; if the impl item is missing or incompatible it returns an error progress.

Confirms an impl-trait-in-trait projection by finding the concrete associated definition with `assoc_def`, normalizing the impl method predicates with `normalize_with_depth_to`, converting them into nested obligations, and normalizing the bound impl-trait result type with `normalize_to` before returning the final projected term and obligations.

Collects and adds the associated item's own declared predicates as nested obligations by instantiating the item's predicates, normalizing each predicate with `normalize_with_depth_to`, choosing an appropriate obligation cause, and pushing each normalized predicate as a deeper obligation.
Trait method contract for deriving a projection-cache key from a poly projection predicate and selection context.

Builds a `ProjectionCacheKey` for a poly projection predicate only when it has no bound vars. It explicitly calls `ProjectionCacheKey::new` after resolving inference variables in the predicate's projection type with `resolve_vars_if_possible`.
Adds the intercrate ambiguity explanation to a diagnostic by calling `intercrate_ambiguity_hint` to build the message and `note` to attach it.
Builds and returns a human-readable ambiguity hint string for each `IntercrateAmbiguityCause` variant, using `String::new` for missing self types and `clone` for reservation-impl messages.

Constructs a fresh `SelectionContext` with standard query mode, recursive inductive-cycle handling, no intercrate ambiguity tracking, and initializes the freshener by calling `freshener` on the inference context.
Constructs a `SelectionContext` with an explicit `TraitQueryMode` by calling `SelectionContext::new` and overriding the `query_mode` field.
Enables collection of intercrate ambiguity causes after asserting intercrate mode with `is_intercrate`, ensuring tracking is not already active, and initializing the set with `default`.
Drains and returns the collected intercrate ambiguity causes after asserting intercrate mode with `is_intercrate`, using `take` and `unwrap_or_default`.
Returns the underlying `TyCtxt` stored in the inference context.
Reports whether this selection context is running in intercrate mode by reading the inference context flag.
Wraps a monomorphic `TraitObligation` into a `PolyTraitObligation` by cloning the cause and using `ty::Binder::dummy`, then calls `poly_select`.

Starts candidate selection for a root obligation by creating a fresh provisional evaluation cache, building the initial stack with `push_stack` over `TraitObligationStackList::empty`, and then calling `candidate_from_obligation`.

Selects a candidate with caching support: it calls `check_recursion_limit`, freshens the predicate with `freshen`, queries cached results via `check_candidate_cache`, and on a miss computes the result by calling `in_task` around `candidate_from_obligation_no_cache` before storing it with `insert_candidate_cache`.

Computes a selection candidate without using the candidate cache. It first calls `is_knowable` to reject intercrate-ambiguous obligations, and in that path may call `assemble_candidates` and `evaluate_candidate` to decide whether to record an `IntercrateAmbiguityCause`. Otherwise it assembles candidates, filters and evaluates them, records ambiguity causes when appropriate, applies `filter_impls` and `filter_reservation_impls`, drops dominated candidates with `candidate_should_be_dropped_in_favor_of`, and returns the unique surviving candidate, ambiguity, or overflow/error as appropriate.

Evaluates a root predicate obligation in a probe by calling `evaluation_probe`, normalizing the goal with `resolve_vars_if_possible`, recursively evaluating it via `evaluate_predicate_recursively` on an empty stack, and downgrading the result with `shallow_resolve` and `max` if inference variables changed.

Runs an evaluation closure inside an inference probe by calling `probe`, executing `op`, then checking soundness and side effects with `universe`, `leak_check`, `opaque_types_added_in_snapshot`, and `region_constraints_added_in_snapshot`, using `max` to weaken the result when needed.

Evaluates a sequence of nested obligations by setting each obligation depth from the parent with `set_depth_from_parent`, calling `evaluate_predicate_recursively` for each one, and combining results with `max` while fast-returning on `EvaluatedToErr`.

Evaluates a batch of predicate obligations with the new solver by creating a fulfillment context via `new`, registering obligations with `register_predicate_obligations`, then calling `select_where_possible` and `select_all_or_error`; it returns `EvaluatedToErr` for immediate errors, `EvaluatedToAmbig` for unresolved obligations, and `EvaluatedToOk` otherwise.

Recursively evaluates a general predicate obligation. It calls `check_recursion_limit` using the current stack head when present, then dispatches by predicate kind inside `ensure_sufficient_stack`: trait predicates are forwarded to `evaluate_trait_predicate_recursively`; subtype and coerce predicates use `subtype_predicate` or `coerce_predicate` and then `evaluate_predicates_recursively`; well-formedness, projection, const-evaluatable, and outlives-related cases evaluate through the corresponding inference or obligation-producing paths; cycle-related paths use `coinductive_match`, `update_reached_depth`, and recursive calls to `evaluate_predicate_recursively`/`evaluate_predicates_recursively` to combine nested results.

Recursively evaluates a trait predicate with caching and cycle handling. It may canonicalize the param-env for better caching, then calls `push_stack`, checks cached results with `check_evaluation_cache` and provisional results with `get_provisional`, detects recursion with `check_evaluation_cycle`, computes a fresh result by calling `in_task` around `evaluate_stack`, may re-normalize and re-evaluate via `try_normalize_with_depth_to`, `evaluate_predicate_recursively`, or recursive `evaluate_trait_predicate_recursively`, and finally stores results with `insert_evaluation_cache` or provisional-cache insertion as appropriate.

Detects whether the current trait obligation forms a cycle with an earlier stack frame by scanning the stack, marking the cycle depth with `update_reached_depth`, building the participating predicate sequence using `tcx` and `to_predicate`, and then calling `coinductive_match`; coinductive cycles evaluate to success, while inductive cycles are converted with `into` from the current cycle policy.

Evaluates a trait-obligation stack frame while guarding against recursive unbound-input loops. It checks for repeated fresh trait references with `match_fresh_trait_refs`, returns ambiguity for that conservative recursion case, otherwise calls `candidate_from_obligation` and then `evaluate_candidate` on the selected candidate.
Returns whether every predicate in a detected cycle is coinductive by calling `is_coinductive` on each predicate with `tcx`.

Evaluates a specific selection candidate by calling `evaluation_probe`, cloning the candidate, confirming it with `confirm_candidate`, recursively evaluating its nested obligations via `evaluate_predicates_recursively`, and then weakening the result with `max` if the freshened trait predicate has erased regions.

Looks up a trait-evaluation result in the caches, first refusing to cache in intercrate mode via `is_intercrate`, then using `tcx`, `can_use_global_caches`, and `get` to query the global cache before falling back to the local inference-context cache.

Stores a completed evaluation result unless it is stack-dependent or intercrate-specific. It checks `is_stack_dependent`, `is_intercrate`, and `can_use_global_caches`; if globally cacheable and inference-free it inserts through `tcx().evaluation_cache.insert`, otherwise it inserts into the local evaluation cache.

Enforces the trait-selection recursion limit by consulting `recursion_limit` and `value_within_limit`; on overflow it either returns a canonical overflow, converts existing taint via `tainted_by_errors`, or reports the overflow using `err_ctxt().report_overflow_obligation`.
Checks the recursion limit for an obligation by delegating directly to `check_recursion_depth` with the obligation's `recursion_depth`.

Executes a selection operation inside an anonymous dep-graph task by calling `tcx().dep_graph.with_anon_task`, then marks the resulting dependency with `read_index` and returns both the result and dep-node index.

Filters a candidate list to keep only impl candidates whose polarity matches the obligation or is reservation-only, using `tcx` to query `impl_polarity`, while passing through non-impl candidates unchanged.

Filters out reservation impl candidates by treating an `ImplCandidate` with reservation polarity as ambiguous; it calls `tcx` to query impl polarity and reservation attributes, records an `IntercrateAmbiguityCause::ReservationImpl` when tracking is enabled, and otherwise returns the original candidate.

Checks whether the current trait obligation is knowable in intercrate mode. It calls `is_intercrate` to fast-path non-intercrate cases, uses `resolve_vars_if_possible` to simplify the predicate, calls `tcx`, and then delegates to `coherence::trait_ref_is_knowable` on the obligation's trait ref.
Determines whether selection may use the global cache: it returns false if the parameter environment has inference variables or if `is_intercrate` is true, and true otherwise.

Looks up a previously computed candidate result in the selection caches. It calls `is_intercrate` to disable caching in intercrate mode, `tcx` and `skip_binder` to form the cache key, then calls `can_use_global_caches` and checks the global cache before falling back to the local inference-context cache.

Determines whether a selection result is safe to cache. It calls `is_intercrate` to reject all intercrate caching, and for `ParamCandidate` results only allows caching when the trait ref has no inference variables.

Stores a candidate result in either the global or local selection cache. It calls `tcx`, `skip_binder`, `can_cache_candidate`, and `can_use_global_caches`; cacheable, inference-free, non-canonical-overflow results go to `tcx.selection_cache`, otherwise they are inserted into the local `infcx.selection_cache`.

Finds definition-bound trait clauses on a projection or opaque self type that can satisfy the given obligation. It calls `resolve_vars_if_possible`, `instantiate_binder_with_placeholders`, and then, for each bound from `item_bounds`, probes by calling `match_normalize_trait_ref`; matching bounds are deduplicated after normalization and their indices are returned.

Normalizes a candidate trait bound and checks whether it can be matched against a placeholder obligation trait ref. It first compares trait `def_id`s, then calls `project::normalize_with_depth` under `ensure_sufficient_stack`, and finally uses `infcx.at(...).sup(...)` to test the match, returning the normalized trait ref only if no inference variables or placeholders remain.

Evaluates whether a where-clause trait ref may satisfy the current stack obligation inside an evaluation probe. It calls `evaluation_probe`, then `match_where_clause_trait_ref`, and on success calls `evaluate_predicates_recursively` with `stack.list()` and the produced obligations.

Tests whether an environment projection predicate can match a projection obligation, optionally normalizing the candidate projection first. It calls `instantiate_binder_with_fresh_vars`, optionally `project::normalize_with_depth_to` via `ensure_sufficient_stack`, then uses `infcx.at(...).sup(...)` and `evaluate_predicates_recursively` to validate nested obligations; on success it calls `tcx` and checks GAT argument inference to distinguish `Yes` from `Ambiguous`.
Constructs `DropVictim::Yes` or `DropVictim::No` directly from the boolean flag; it does not call other methods in this methods list.

Applies the candidate-priority and specialization rules used during winnowing to decide whether one evaluated candidate should be dropped in favor of another. It calls `DropVictim::drop_if` for several tie-breakers, and also consults `must_apply_modulo_regions`, `tcx`, `specializes`, `impls_are_allowed_to_overlap`, and `must_apply_considering_regions` when comparing impl, object, projection, upcasting, and param candidates.

Computes the builtin `Sized` conditions for the obligation's self type after `shallow_resolve`. Primitive, pointer, reference, closure, coroutine, and similar sized types yield an empty `Where`; tuples require the last element; ADTs call `tcx` and `sized_constraint`/`iter_instantiated` to derive field constraints; unsized aliases/params/placeholders return `None`, and unresolved type vars return `Ambiguous`.

Computes builtin `Copy`/`Clone` conditions for the obligation's self type after `shallow_resolve`. It returns fixed answers for primitive/reference cases, builds tuple obligations from all elements, calls `tcx().features()` for movable coroutine clone support, uses coroutine accessors and `shallow_resolve` to derive coroutine requirements, and uses `bind_coroutine_hidden_types_above` for coroutine witnesses.

Extracts the constituent types that must satisfy an auto trait for a given type. It returns empty constituents for primitives, calls `tcx` to model `str` as `[u8]` and to read ADT field types, uses `shallow_resolve` for closure and coroutine upvars, and calls `bind_coroutine_hidden_types_above` for coroutine witnesses; unsupported unresolved or abstract forms trigger bugs.

Builds trait obligations for each type in a binder-aware list, preserving higher-ranked structure by instantiating placeholders and rebinding afterward. For each type it calls `instantiate_binder_with_placeholders`, `project::normalize_with_depth` under `ensure_sufficient_stack`, uses `tcx`/`generics_of` to construct the trait ref (or error args for malformed traits), and then creates an `Obligation` plus any normalization obligations.

Re-runs impl matching for a previously selected impl candidate. It calls `tcx().impl_trait_ref(...).unwrap()` and then `match_impl`; if rematching fails, it emits a delayed span bug, calls `fresh_args_for_item`, creates an error type with `Ty::new_error`, folds the fresh args to errors, and returns a `Normalized` result with no obligations.

Attempts to match an impl's trait ref against the current obligation. It calls `instantiate_binder_with_placeholders`, `fresh_args_for_item`, `tcx`, and `project::normalize_with_depth` under `ensure_sufficient_stack`, then uses `infcx.at(...).eq(...)` to equate the impl and obligation trait refs; finally it calls `is_intercrate` and `tcx().impl_polarity(...)` to reject reservation impls outside intercrate mode.
Matches a where-clause trait ref against the obligation by directly calling `match_poly_trait_ref` and returning its obligations.

Checks whether a polymorphic trait ref can satisfy the obligation by calling `infcx.at(...).sup(...)` between `obligation.predicate.to_poly_trait_ref()` and the candidate trait ref, returning the generated obligations on success.
Compares two freshened trait predicates for structural compatibility by constructing `MatchAgainstFreshVars::new(self.tcx(), param_env)` and calling `relate(...).is_ok()`.

Pushes a new obligation onto the recursion stack by freshening the predicate with `fold_with`, obtaining a new depth-first number via `next_dfn`, reading the previous `depth`, and constructing a new `TraitObligationStack` node.

Builds the unnormalized closure trait ref corresponding to a closure obligation. It reads the closure signature from `args.as_closure().sig()`, extracts the self type from the obligation, then calls `closure_trait_ref_and_return_type(self.tcx(), ...)` and maps the result to just the trait ref.

Instantiates and normalizes all predicates declared on an impl or trait, producing nested obligations in dependency order. It calls `tcx`, `predicates_of`, and `instantiate_own`, derives obligation causes (except for `CoerceUnsized`), then for each predicate calls `normalize_with_depth_to` and pushes the resulting normalized clause as an `Obligation`.
Returns a `TraitObligationStackList` view for this stack by calling `TraitObligationStackList::with(self)`.
Returns the provisional evaluation cache stored in the previous stack list; it does not call other methods in this methods list.
Returns an iterator-like stack list by directly calling `self.list()`.

Marks all stack frames above a given cycle depth as having participated in that cycle. It walks through `previous.head`, updating each frame's `reached_depth` cell with `min`, until the target depth is reached.
Constructs an empty provisional evaluation cache by initializing the DFN cell to 0 and using `Default::default()` for the internal maps; it does not call other methods in this methods list.
Returns the current DFN counter and increments it for the next use. It calls `get` to read the current counter value and `set` to store the incremented value.

Looks up and returns a copied provisional evaluation for the given fresh trait predicate from the cache map, or `None` if absent. It calls `borrow` to immutably access the map and `get` to perform the lookup.

Updates cached provisional entries whose `from_dfn` depends on the current frame so their `reached_depth` is conservatively lowered, then inserts the new provisional evaluation for the fresh trait predicate. It calls `borrow_mut` to mutate the cache map, `min` to merge depths, and `insert` to store the new entry.

Removes provisional cache entries during unwinding after a failed evaluation, retaining only entries that should survive past the given DFN threshold. It calls `borrow_mut` to mutably access the cache map and `retain` to filter entries in place.

Clears provisional cache entries created at or below the completed DFN once evaluation finishes successfully. It calls `borrow_mut` to mutably access the cache map and `retain` to discard matching entries.
Constructs an empty obligation stack list for the given provisional evaluation cache, with no head stack frame.
Constructs a stack list whose head is the given obligation stack and whose cache is taken from that stack. It explicitly calls `TraitObligationStack::cache` via `r.cache()`.
Returns the current head obligation stack frame, if any.
Returns the depth of the current head obligation stack frame, or `0` when the list is empty.
Advances iteration over the obligation stack list by returning the current head frame and replacing the list with that frame's previous link.
Formats a `TraitObligationStack` for debugging by writing its wrapped obligation in a `TraitObligationStack(...)` wrapper.

Builds a binder for a generator's hidden types by fetching hidden types with `generator_hidden_types`, deduplicating them with `filter` and `insert`, instantiating each with `subst`, optionally remapping erased regions via `fold_regions`, `kind`, `from_u32`, `BrAnon`, and `mk_re_late_bound`, then collecting the types with `collect`, extending bound variables using `mk_bound_variable_kinds_from_iter`, `iter`, `chain`, `map`, and `Region`, and finally returning the binder with `bind_with_vars`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_analysis/src/check/ch: Validates that an ABI is supported on the current target, emitting a hard error for unsupported ABIs and a lint for target-dependent unsupported calling conventions. It does not call other listed methods.

Performs item-level checks for a struct by forcing destructor evaluation, conditionally calling `check_simd` for SIMD structs, and always calling `check_transparent`, `check_packed`, and `check_unnamed_fields`.
Performs item-level checks for a union by forcing destructor evaluation and then calling `check_transparent`, `check_union_fields`, `check_packed`, and `check_unnamed_fields`.

Checks each union field after normalization and accepts only references, recursively permitted tuples/arrays, `ManuallyDrop`, `Copy`, or erroneous types; otherwise emits an invalid-union-field error. It calls the nested helper `allowed_union_field` to recursively classify field types.

Recursively decides whether a type is legal as a union field: references are accepted, tuples and arrays are checked recursively, and other types are accepted only if they are `ManuallyDrop`, `Copy`, or already erroneous. It calls itself recursively for tuple elements and array elements.

Computes the layout of a static to reject oversized foreign statics and lint uninhabited static types, while treating unexpected layout failures as delayed bugs. It does not call other listed methods.

Validates an opaque type item by confirming it is an opaque HIR item, skipping rustdoc, bailing out on erroneous hidden types, then calling `check_opaque_for_cycles` and, if that succeeds, `check_opaque_meets_bounds`.

Checks that an opaque type definition does not capture parent lifetimes or illicit `Self` references from its surrounding context, walking both the HIR item and the opaque’s explicit bounds. It calls `expect_item` to fetch the HIR item, `mk_opaque`, `identity_for_item`, `generics_of`, and `explicit_item_bounds` to construct and inspect the opaque identity and bounds, uses `visit_item`, `visit_with`, and `break_value` through local visitors to detect forbidden lifetime capture, uses `def_path_str` while recording `Self`-type references, and reports diagnostics via `span_suggestion`, `unwrap_or_else`, `map_break`, and `emit`.
Supplies the HIR map used for nested body traversal by this visitor. It calls `hir` to obtain that map from the type context.

Walks HIR type syntax to collect `Self` type references that are illegal to capture inside the opaque definition, recording either plain `Self` or aliased `Self` paths. It calls `def_path_str` to name aliased `Self` targets, `push` to record each match, and `walk_ty` to continue recursive HIR traversal.

Detects invalid recursive opaque expansions by trying impl-trait expansion with and without coroutine fields, reporting a true opaque cycle via `opaque_type_cycle_error`, and otherwise checking for coroutine layout cycles. It calls `opaque_type_cycle_error` when a real expansion cycle is found.

Builds an inference and obligation context for an opaque type, relates the declared opaque to its hidden type under the proper parameter environment, registers well-formedness and bound obligations, and reports fulfillment or region-resolution errors if the hidden type does not satisfy the opaque's bounds. It does not call other listed methods.

Recognizes the special two-variant nullable-pointer optimization shape: an enum without inhibited layout optimization where one variant is empty and the other contains exactly one function-pointer or reference field. It does not call other listed methods.

Checks that a static with import linkage has an allowed representation, permitting raw pointers and nullable-pointer-optimized enums while rejecting other types. It calls `is_enum_of_nonnullable_ptr` for ADT statics.

Dispatches item-type validation by `DefKind`: for statics it calls `check_static_inhabited` and `check_static_linkage`; for enums it calls `check_enum`; for trait impls it calls `check_impl_items_against_trait` and `check_on_unimplemented` when coherence succeeds; for traits it calls `check_on_unimplemented`; for structs it calls `check_struct`; for unions it calls `check_union`; and for opaque types it calls `check_opaque_precise_captures` before further opaque-origin-specific validation. This is the central coordinator for the file’s item-level checks.
Forces evaluation of a trait or impl item's `#[rustc_on_unimplemented]` directive so any diagnostic errors are reported. It does not call other listed methods.

Walks ancestor impls to determine whether an impl item is allowed to specialize a trait item, rejecting specialization when the inherited parent item is final or comes from a non-default ancestor impl. It does not call other listed methods.

Checks each impl item against its corresponding trait item, dispatching to the appropriate impl-vs-trait comparison and then calling `check_specialization_validity`; it also performs follow-up validation for missing items and inherited defaults across trait ancestors. It calls `check_specialization_validity` for every matched impl item.

Validates a SIMD struct by requiring at least one field, homogeneous element types, a legal lane count, and scalar-or-pointer lane element kinds (or generic forms deferred to monomorphization). It does not call other listed methods.

Validates `repr(packed)` usage by rejecting conflicting packed hints or `packed`+`align`, and otherwise checking for transitive containment of `repr(align)` types. It calls `check_packed_inner` to search nested field types for aligned ADTs.

Recursively searches a struct/union and its nested ADT fields for a `repr(align)` type while tracking a stack to avoid cycles, returning the path of offending definitions and field spans when found. It calls itself recursively on nested ADT field types.

Validates `repr(transparent)` ADTs by enforcing the feature gate for transparent unions, requiring exactly one variant, computing which fields are trivial 1-ZSTs, and rejecting invalid transparent layouts including problematic non-exhaustive/private external ZST contents. It calls the nested helper `check_non_exhaustive` to recursively inspect field types for disallowed external non-exhaustive/private structure.

Recursively inspects a type used in a transparent field and stops when it finds a non-local ADT whose variant/field set is non-exhaustive or contains private fields; tuples, arrays, and nested ADT fields are traversed recursively. It calls itself recursively for tuple elements, array elements, and nested ADT field types.

Performs enum validation by forcing destructor evaluation, rejecting `repr` on zero-variant enums, feature-gating `repr(i128/u128)`, type-checking explicit discriminants, enforcing `#[repr(inttype)]` when mixed explicit discriminants require it, then calling `detect_discriminant_duplicate` and `check_transparent`.

Detects duplicate enum discriminant values and builds detailed diagnostics that explain whether the duplicate was explicit, overflow-derived, or inherited from a prior explicit discriminant. It does not call other listed methods.

Verifies that all type parameters declared on a top-level generic item are actually used in the item type, suppressing the check if the type already contains an error. It calls `own_counts` and `len` to size the tracking set, `references_error`, `has_errors`, and `is_some` to short-circuit on prior errors, `walk`, `unpack`, and `kind` to inspect type leaves, `insert` and `contains` to track used parameters, `def_span` to locate unused ones, and `span_label` plus `emit` to report E0091.
Checks every item type in a module by iterating over the module’s HIR items. It calls `hir_module_items`, `items`, and `check_item_type`.

Emits the dedicated recursion error for an `async fn` whose opaque future type forms a cycle and therefore requires boxing. It calls `span_label`, `note`, and `emit` to build and issue the diagnostic.

Constructs the diagnostic for an opaque-type recursion error by examining return paths, distinguishing pure-`!` returns from recursive opaque uses, and tracing recursive references through nested opaque types and closures/coroutines. It uses the nested `OpaqueTypeCollector::visit_ty` visitor to collect opaque and closure/coroutine references from return types.

Visits a type while collecting nested opaque aliases and closure/coroutine types for opaque-cycle diagnostics, and recursively descends into substructure with `super_visit_with`. It does not call other listed methods from this file.

Visits a type while prohibiting references from an opaque type to parent regions. If the visited type is the opaque identity type, it immediately continues; otherwise it calls `visit_with` using `ConstrainOpaqueTypeRegionVisitor` to scan regions, marks when an early-bound parent region (`ReEarlyBound`) is referenced, and returns `Break` with the offending type or `Continue` if no forbidden parent-region reference is found.

Checks that a generator's interior predicates are satisfiable after type checking. It calls `def_kind` and `typeck` to validate and fetch type-check results, `param_env` to obtain the parameter environment, then builds an inference context by calling `infer_ctxt`, `ignoring_regions`, `with_opaque_type_inference`, and `build`. It creates a trait engine with `new`, constructs obligations with `Obligation::new` using cloned causes, registers them via `register_predicate_obligation`, resolves them with `select_all_or_error`, and if any errors remain, reports them by calling `err_ctxt` and `report_fulfillment_errors`.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_hir_typeck/src/check.rs::: Type-checks a function body by preparing the `FnCtxt` state, replacing opaque return types with inference variables, forbidding invalid intrinsic ABIs, gathering locals, checking parameter patterns and well-formedness, enforcing sizedness constraints, checking the body, and reconciling the coerced body result with the declared return type; it explicitly calls `forbid_intrinsic_abi` and uses `GatherLocalsVisitor::new(...).visit_body(...)` to collect locals before parameter/body checking.

Validates that the panic handler lang item has the required non-generic function form by constructing the expected `for<'a, 'b> fn(&'a PanicInfo<'b>) -> !` signature and explicitly calling `check_function_signature` to compare it against the actual signature.

Validates the `start` lang item signature by building the expected `fn(main: fn() -> T, argc: isize, argv: *const *const u8, sigpipe: u8) -> isize` form and explicitly calling `check_function_signature` to enforce it.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_middle/src/ty/opaque_type: Constructs a `ReverseMapper` from the type context, remapping table, diagnostic span, and error-suppression flag, initializing `do_not_error` to `false`. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Temporarily enables the `do_not_error` mode, folds a generic argument through this mapper, and then restores normal error behavior. It calls `fold_with` on the argument, which routes folding back through this `TypeFolder` implementation.

Folds a generic argument through the mapper under normal diagnostics, requiring that missing-region suppression is not active. It calls `fold_with` on the argument, which uses this `TypeFolder` implementation.

Remaps a closure-like item's substitutions into the opaque type's parameter space, treating parent-generic arguments specially so missing parent regions do not immediately error. It calls `generics_of` to inspect the closure's generic layout, `mk_substs_from_iter` to rebuild the substitution list, `fold_kind_no_missing_regions_error` for arguments in the parent-generic prefix, and `fold_kind_normally` for the remaining arguments.
Returns the `TyCtxt` interner stored in the mapper. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.

Remaps regions used in an opaque hidden type: it leaves bound, static, erased, and error regions unchanged, expects early/late parameter regions to be in the reverse map, substitutes `'static` when missing-region diagnostics are suppressed, and otherwise emits an error and returns an error region. When constructing the error region, it calls `interner` from the Methods List.

Remaps types inside the hidden type: it specially reconstructs closures, coroutines, and coroutine witnesses with rewritten generic arguments, remaps type parameters through the reverse map, reports unmapped parameters, and otherwise recursively folds substructure. It calls `fold_closure_args` for `Closure`, `Coroutine`, and `CoroutineWitness` cases.

Remaps const generic parameters through the reverse map, emits `ConstNotUsedTraitAlias` and returns an error const when a const parameter is not listed in the opaque type parameters, and leaves non-parameter consts unchanged. It does not call other methods from the Methods List.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/opaque_types: Constructs a fresh `OpaqueTypeCollector` for the given item, initializing an empty opaque list and a default `seen` set. Calls `Default::default` to initialize `seen`.

Returns the current diagnostic span, falling back to the item's identifier span and then its full definition span when no explicit span is being tracked. Calls `def_ident_span` and, if needed, `def_span` through nested `unwrap_or_else` fallbacks.
Temporarily installs a source span while visiting a type-visitable value, then restores the previous span afterward. Calls `visit_with` on the provided value.

Finds the enclosing impl trait reference for the current associated item, returning it only when the parent is an impl. Calls `parent`; if present, it queries `def_kind`, then calls `impl_trait_ref` and `instantiate_identity`.
Returns the local parent of the current item when the item is an associated function, type, or const; otherwise returns `None`. Calls `def_kind` and, for associated items, `local_parent`.

Traverses a type and handles aliases specially for opaque-type collection: it first recurses into substructure, then records local opaque aliases, expands local weak aliases to their underlying type, and tries to resolve same-impl associated-type projections so their concrete types can also be visited. Calls `super_visit_with`; for local opaque aliases it calls `visit_opaque_ty`; for local weak aliases it calls `type_of`, `instantiate`, and `visit_with`; for projection aliases it calls `parent_trait_ref`, `parent`, `associated_items`, `in_definition_order`, `defaultness`, `is_final`, `rebase_onto`, `identity_for_item`, `check_args_compatible`, and on success `type_of`, `instantiate`, and `visit_with`, while mismatch/error paths use `dcx`, `span_delayed_bug`, and `def_span`. It also visits instantiated variant field types in the ADT-related branch via `variants`, `iter`, `instantiate_identity`, and `visit_spanned`.

Computes the opaque types an item may define by creating an `OpaqueTypeCollector`, walking the item's signature types, optionally collecting TAITs declared in the body for body-checked items, and inheriting parent opaques for closures/inline consts before interning the result. Calls `def_kind`, `OpaqueTypeCollector::new`, `walk_types`, `collect_taits_declared_in_body`, `opaque_types_defined_by` recursively for the parent of closures/inline consts, `local_parent`, `extend`, and `mk_local_def_ids`.
Registers this file's query providers by installing `opaque_types_defined_by` and `impl_trait_in_assoc_types_defined_by` into the `Providers` table.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_monomorphize/src/collecto: Constructs an empty `UsageMap` by initializing both internal hash maps with their defaults.
Records the dependency edges for one mono item by collecting the used `MonoItem`s, updating `user_map` with reverse edges, and inserting the forward edge list into `used_map`.
Returns the mono items that use the given item by reading `user_map`, or an empty slice if none are recorded.
Iterates over the recorded used items for a mono item and invokes the callback only for dependencies whose `instantiation_mode` is `LocalCopy`.

Main entry point for crate-wide monomorphization collection: it calls `collect_roots` to find initial roots, creates a fresh `UsageMap` with `UsageMap::new`, then traverses each root in parallel by calling `collect_items_rec`, finally returning the visited mono items and usage graph.

Collects initial mono-item roots from HIR by visiting crate items and impl items through `RootCollector::process_item`, `RootCollector::process_impl_item`, and `RootCollector::push_extra_entry_roots`, then filters the results to only instantiable mono items.

Recursively walks the monomorphization graph from one starting item, skipping already-visited nodes, discovering directly used items from statics/functions/MIR, checking recursion and type-size limits, recursing into discovered dependencies, and recording edges in the `UsageMap` with `UsageMap::record_used`. In this method, notable calls to methods from the list include `should_codegen_locally`, `visit_drop_use`, `check_recursion_limit`, `check_type_length_limit`, and `visit_fn_use`.
Builds a shorter printable instance name for diagnostics, and if shortening changes the text, writes the full long name to a temporary file and returns that path.

Checks and updates per-definition monomorphization recursion depth, applying special handling for `drop_in_place`; if the adjusted depth exceeds the limit, it calls `shrunk_instance_name` to prepare diagnostic text and then emits a fatal recursion-limit error.
Computes the generic type/const argument expansion size for an instance and, if it exceeds the configured limit, calls `shrunk_instance_name` and emits a fatal type-length-limit error.
Monomorphizes and normalizes a MIR-related value under the collector’s current instance using reveal-all parameter environment.

Examines MIR rvalues for codegen-relevant uses such as unsizing casts, reified fn pointers, closure fn pointers, and thread-local statics. It calls `MirUsedCollector::monomorphize` to obtain concrete types, `find_vtable_types_for_unsizing` and `create_mono_items_for_vtable_methods` for trait-object unsizing, `visit_fn_use` for function-pointer uses, and `create_fn_mono_item` when a closure shim must be emitted.

Evaluates a monomorphized MIR constant and collects mono items reachable from its value; it calls `MirUsedCollector::monomorphize` and then `collect_const_value`, and finally visits the constant’s type.

Handles terminators that imply codegen dependencies: calls/functions, drops, inline asm symbol references, panic/assert lang items, and unwind handlers. It calls `MirUsedCollector::monomorphize`, `MirUsedCollector::check_fn_args_move_size`, `visit_fn_use`, `visit_drop_use`, and `create_fn_mono_item` as needed to enqueue referenced mono items.
Performs the default operand traversal and then calls `MirUsedCollector::check_operand_move_size` to lint oversized operand moves.
No-op `MirVisitor` hook for local-place visits; it intentionally performs no collection work and does not call other methods in this file.
Resolves the `drop_in_place` instance for a type and forwards it to `visit_instance_use` for mono-item collection.
Collects a function use when the type is `FnDef` by resolving the concrete instance for either a direct call or a reified fn pointer, then calling `visit_instance_use`.

Decides whether and how a resolved instance contributes a mono item: it first calls `should_codegen_locally`, rejects impossible reifications, skips direct no-op drop glue, and otherwise pushes a function mono item via `create_fn_mono_item` for the instance kinds that require code generation.

Determines whether an instance must be code generated in the current crate by excluding foreign items, upstream-linkable or already-upstream-monomorphized items, upstream statics, and by emitting a fatal error when required MIR is unavailable.

Finds the concrete source/target types that determine vtable generation for an unsizing coercion, handling references, raw pointers, boxes, dyn* coercions, and recursive field-based custom unsizing; it may call itself recursively for nested struct-field coercions.
Builds a `MonoItem::Fn` for an instance, optionally dumping closure profiling data for local closures before returning the spanned mono item.

Creates mono items required for a trait-object vtable by enumerating vtable method entries, filtering them with `should_codegen_locally`, mapping them through `create_fn_mono_item`, extending the output with those methods, and then calling `visit_drop_use` to add the destructor.

Processes one HIR item as a possible monomorphization root: eager non-generic ADTs add drop glue via `visit_drop_use`, global asm/statics are pushed directly, consts are scanned with `collect_const_value`, eager impls call `create_mono_items_for_default_impls`, and functions are forwarded to `RootCollector::push_if_root`.
Treats associated functions in impls as potential roots by calling `RootCollector::push_if_root`.

Checks whether a local function-like item qualifies as a root by requiring no monomorphization-needed generics and then applying eager-vs-lazy root rules based on entry-point, reachability, or special codegen attributes.
Adds a local definition as a root only if `RootCollector::is_root` returns true, creating the corresponding mono item with `create_fn_mono_item`.
For a `main` entry point, resolves the lang-item `start` wrapper instantiated with `main`’s return type and pushes it as an additional root by calling `create_fn_mono_item`.
Returns whether a local item has generics that require monomorphization. It calls `tcx.generics_of` to fetch the item’s generics and then `requires_monomorphization` on that generics object.

Eagerly instantiates default trait methods for non-negative, non-generic impls whose predicates are satisfiable, skipping overridden methods and only pushing methods that are instantiable and locally codegened. In this process it calls `should_codegen_locally` and `create_fn_mono_item` for each selected default method.

Collects mono-item uses reachable from an instance's MIR by running the MIR used-item visitor. It calls `instance_mir` to fetch the body and then invokes `visit_body` on `MirUsedCollector` to discover and record referenced items.

Collects mono items referenced by a constant value's allocation-backed contents. It calls `collect_alloc` for pointer scalars, indirect allocations, and every provenance pointer found inside slice data, while ignoring constant forms with no embedded allocation references.

Traverses a global allocation and collects codegen-relevant mono items reachable from it. It calls `collect_miri` recursively for nested provenance pointers in `GlobalAlloc::Memory` and again after resolving a `GlobalAlloc::VTable` through `vtable_allocation`; for `GlobalAlloc::Static` and `GlobalAlloc::Function`, it checks `should_codegen_locally` and then pushes the corresponding mono item into the output.
method_docs.compiler/rustc_ty_utils/src/instance.rs:: Resolves a `(DefId, GenericArgsRef)` into a concrete `Instance` by first splitting the query key with `into_parts`.
